q: Describe the pattern for red blood cells.
The rate rises steeply at low concentrations, then levels off near 98–99 above about 10–20 mmol dm⁻³.
Explain why the rate for red blood cells levels off.
Every carrier protein (GLUT1) is already working as fast as it can: the carriers are saturated, so their number limits the rate.
Compare the red blood cells with the lipid bilayer and explain the difference.

The bilayer is far slower (6 against 99 at 30 mmol dm⁻³) and its rate rises in a straight line with no levelling off. Glucose is large and polar, so it barely crosses the phospholipids; carrier proteins give it a route.
Calculate how many times faster uptake is by the cells than through the bilayer at 10 mmol dm⁻³.
Explain why this uptake is not active transport.
It only happens down the concentration gradient (zero when outside glucose is zero) and does not need ATP: it is facilitated diffusion.
